source_integrity.summary: Checked core archaeology: Kuijt/Finlayson Dhra 2009; Zheng/Crawford Lower Yangtze rice shattering 2016 (77 wild,38 intermediate,11 nonshattering bases); Wang 2022 rice tools; Denham Kuk 2003 phases; Burgarella pearl-millet genomics 2018; UNESCO Çatalhöyük and Kuk; Twiss et al. 2024 and Kohler et al. 2025 inequality; Cox et al. 2022 early farmers; Casanova et al. 2026 dairy.

factual_methodology.summary: Separates gathering, cultivation, morphological domestication, sedentism, storage, herd management and centralized states. Heterogeneous early evidence in chart expressly labeled non-equivalent; no fabricated tax/GDP, wealth or universal progress metric.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: Research cutoff 3 November 2026; earliest selected dates are approximate context-specific BP or calibrated BP; 2024 Çatalhöyük inequality, 2025 PNAS comparative inequality and 2026 Zagros dairy study separately attributed.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: 19 connected argumentative chapters before bibliography, international comparison across ecology, labor, health, demography, politics and alternative causal mechanisms; substantive EN/PT-BR well above required 8,000 prose characters.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two matching evidentiary chronology charts per locale with six marker ages and three Kuk-phase boundaries, two comparative tables, one three-chain causal diagram and one multi-region map; all ages and methodological limits labelled.

research_depth.summary: English about 4,947 substantive words and Portuguese about 5,265, with substantive comparative economic, political and social analysis, case-level source-specific evidence and conditional conclusions.

evidence_traceability.summary: 23 matching academic/institutional bibliographic URLs per language across eight hosts. Principal dated, quantitative and inequality claims verified against published abstracts/full open sources; not every entire monograph or publisher-restricted article individually retrieved.

bilingual_parity.summary: Same 20 top-level ## sections including references, 23 matching exact URLs, two identical numeric series, bilingual map, tables and flow, and consistent evidence-versus-inference qualifications.

counterfactual_review.summary: Discusses alternative pathways to inequality through demographic scale, land scarcity, prior ritual rank, warfare and institutional enforcement; distinguishes paths where storage precedes domestication and where dense farming settlement lacks enduring elite hierarchy.

contrary_evidence: Dhra granaries precede the archaeological evidence of fully domesticated cereals, so storage, sedentism and domestication cannot be assumed synchronous.
Çatalhöyük's multi-proxy study finds no unified trajectory of lasting institutionalized hierarchy, contradicting an agricultural-equals-permanent-elite law.
Cross-cultural inequality study finds marked increases often lagged plant domestication by 1,000 years or more, with population/land constraints relevant.
The Kuk Swamp record shows early exploitation, later mounds and much later ditches rather than a single invention moment.
Huxi early rice spikelet bases contain 61.2% wild shattering, 30.1% intermediate and 8.7% domesticated-type bases, undermining instant completed domestication.
Present-day inferred origins and prehistoric archaeological first occurrences have heterogeneous dates, contexts and biological criteria.
limitations: Dates are site-specific and often calibrated BP; model-estimated pearl-millet expansion is not commensurable with an archaeological first appearance.
The cross-regional chronological chart compares selected indicative markers, not comparable dates of full domestication or quantitative productivity.
No prehistoric GDP, tax rates, global population series or directly observed income Gini values are claimed.
Skeletal proxies of health and workload capture selected people and cannot establish universal wellbeing changes.
DNA ancestry and domestication traits cannot by themselves identify ownership, legal entitlements or political coercion.
Review uses published source materials and secondary institutional summaries; it is not an independent peer-reviewed archaeological monograph.
Full external peer review was not conducted; editorial fact-check relied on selective direct source and abstract verification.
All-pending strict editorial-health workflow contains unrelated older backlog quality failures; this SHA-bound study meets the document's separate quantitative and visual checks.
Final build and deployment are separately verified by Actions; a GitHub commit is not proof of domain availability.
notes: Review of exact pending and both source blobs at main head, after original manuscript creation; SHAs locked. Documentary and numeric cross-language checks passed; source verification sampled with explicit limitation. No direct publication by producer; publisher must promote the immutable approved snapshot.

en.title: The Neolithic transformations: cultivation, domestication, surplus and the changing architecture of power
en.deck: A comparative economic, political and social history of cultivation, domestication, storage and authority across the Levant, China, New Guinea, Africa and the Americas, with direct archaeological evidence and rival interpretations.
en.regime: Multiple regional processes restructured harvest risk, labor, land access, household storage and the potential for coercive surplus capture without an inevitable state-forming sequence.
en.key_risk: Mistaking archaeological storage for taxation, domesticates for complete farming packages, cross-regional earliest-date indicators for a single calendar of invention or material wealth proxies for measured incomes.
watch: Independent dating and genetic evidence for early crop management
Household access to stored harvests and inequality proxies
Sex- and age-specific skeletal labor burdens
New paleogenetic evidence of animal management and dairying
en.search_text: neolithic origins of agriculture political economy farming plant domestication crop centers maize millet rice New Guinea Kuk Swamp grain surplus storage property inequality labor disease fertility archaeology

pt-BR.title: As transformações neolíticas: cultivo, domesticação, excedentes e a nova arquitetura do poder
pt-BR.deck: História comparada econômica, política e social do cultivo, domesticação, armazenagem e autoridade no Levante, China, Nova Guiné, África e Américas, com evidência arqueológica e interpretações concorrentes.
pt-BR.regime: Processos regionais distintos reorganizaram o risco de colheitas, o trabalho, o acesso à terra, os estoques domésticos e a capacidade potencial de capturar excedentes sem formação inevitável de Estados.
pt-BR.key_risk: Confundir armazenagem arqueológica com tributação, organismos domesticados com agricultura plenamente estabelecida, datas de evidências diversas com invenções universais ou proxies materiais com renda medida.
watch: Novas datações e evidências genéticas de manejo vegetal
Direitos sobre estoques e indicadores de desigualdade
Carga física por sexo e idade em esqueletos
Novos resultados paleogenéticos de rebanhos e uso de leite

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 3 November 2026 BRT. Source papers 2003–2026, including 2024 Çatalhöyük inequality, 2025 cross-regional wealth comparison and February 2026 Iranian dairy evidence.
producer_checks.editorial_novelty: Third independent study in Civilizations, Economics & Power: agricultural origins, domestication and changing surplus/power mechanisms rather than first Paleolithic toolmaking or preagricultural territorial institutions.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Two bilingual-matched quantitative chronology charts: [11.3,10,9.4,8.7,6.95,4.9] thousand years BP for regional indicators of heterogeneous types and [10.22,6.95,4.35] thousand cal BP for Kuk phases; two evidence comparison tables, one three-chain causal diagram and one ten-region contextual map.
producer_checks.source_check: 23 matching scholarly/institutional URLs in both locales; verified key numbers against PNAS Dhra granaries, Scientific Reports early rice spikelets, Science Kuk sequence, UNESCO Çatalhöyük, PLOS 2024 and PNAS 2025 inequality and Nature Human Behaviour 2026 dairy study.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: 19 equivalent analytical chapters plus bibliography; 23 matching URLs, identical chart values and observations; visual types and competing interpretations substantively equivalent.
producer_checks.research_depth: English 4,947 substantive words / 39,484 characters; Brazilian Portuguese 5,265 substantive words / 41,820 characters, both substantially exceeding 8,000 substantive characters.
producer_checks.methodology: Distinguishes plant collection, cultivation, morphological domestication, animal management, sedentism, household storage, institutional coercion and state formation; case-specific BP/cal BP/BCE chronology, historical alternatives and source provenance.
